html:
Norte Chico is the name for the oldest known civilisation in the Americas, which grew up on the north central coast of Peru from about 3500 BCE to 1800 BCE. The map shows it from 3000 to 2000 BCE. The chart's bar for it is Caral Supe.

Its people built some thirty centres in a cluster of small river valleys, the Supe, Pativilca, Fortaleza and Huaura, a few hours' walk from the Pacific. The largest, Caral, has six big platform mounds and sunken circular plazas, built at the same time as the pyramids of Egypt. The site was excavated from the 1990s by the archaeologist Ruth Shady.

The economy joined sea and valley. Coastal villages caught anchovies and sardines with cotton nets, and inland farmers grew cotton, squash and beans with simple irrigation, then traded. They made almost no pottery, and no signs of war have been found. A knotted string device found at Caral may be an early ancestor of the Inca quipu. Later Andean cultures such as Chavín built on its tradition of temple mounds.
